title: Security information registration is not protected

messages.businessImpact: Anyone holding a stolen password can add a sign-in method of their own to the account, and from then on the multi-factor challenges the rest of the tenant relies on are answered by them rather than by the user.
messages.technicalDetail: A protecting policy must be enabled, target the Register security information user action, and require multi-factor authentication, an authentication strength or a block, with every named control required rather than offered as an alternative. Registering or joining a device is ENR-017's question.
remediation: Create an enabled Conditional Access policy for the Register security information user action that requires multi-factor authentication, or blocks the action outside trusted locations.
Give new starters who have no method yet a Temporary Access Pass rather than leaving registration open.
Exclude emergency access accounts and protect them another way.
messages.cannotSee: Who the policy covers is not compared with the directory, so a policy over some users counts although it may leave guests or contractors open. A block limited to untrusted locations counts however wide the trusted locations are. The Authentication Methods policy and Temporary Access Pass settings are not read.
